Fit a Seymour -> octo registration

fit_seymour_octo_reg.Rd

Affine fit from landmarks, then a coarse-to-fine non-rigid warp that pulls the Seymour synapse cloud onto the octo synapse cloud while keeping the landmarks in place.

Usage

fit_seymour_octo_reg(
  landmarks,
  octo_xyz,
  seymour_xyz,
  holdout = NULL,
  cell = 2000,
  sigma = c(24000, 12000, 6000, 3000),
  iter = c(6, 6, 5, 4),
  trim = c(12000, 8000, 5000, 3000),
  landmark_weight = 1000,
  regularise = 5,
  cv_folds = 0
)

Arguments

landmarks

output of read_seymour_octo_landmarks()

octo_xyz

octo synapse positions (n x 3, nm), e.g. presynaptic positions from octo_synapse_positions()

seymour_xyz

Seymour connector positions (n x 3, nm), e.g. from seymour_connectors()

holdout

landmark rows not used for fitting, only to measure the error

cell

downsampling grid (nm)

sigma, iter, trim

smoothing width (nm), iterations and maximum matching distance (nm) per level

landmark_weight

how many cloud points each landmark counts as

regularise

pulls the warp towards zero where there are few points

cv_folds

if > 0, also estimate the error by k-fold cross-validation over landmarks (takes cv_folds times longer)

Value

a seymour_octo_reg object; save with saveRDS()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
lm  <- read_seymour_octo_landmarks("seymour_octo_reg.csv")
syn <- octo_synapse_positions()
con <- readRDS("seymour_connectors.rds")
reg <- fit_seymour_octo_reg(lm, syn[, c("pre_pt_position_x", "pre_pt_position_y",
                                        "pre_pt_position_z")], con[, c("x", "y", "z")])
saveRDS(reg, "seymour_octo_reg.rds")
} # }
